**Where we are ahead:** the only codec surveyed that types the SPB Instance sub-TLV (CIST root, bridge priority, SPSourceID, ECT-VID tuples) *and* the SPBM-SI with per-I-SID T/R bits (holo has SPBM-SI only — verified in `tlv.rs`; goisis/mdlayher do not mention SPB — *inferred*); zero-allocation bounded decode with a fuzz target that measurably reaches a PDU body; PDUs pinned against an independent dissector; LSP + CSNP + PSNP + both IIH variants in both directions (mdlayher covers the P2P hello only). **Where we are behind:** typed IP reachability only for the wide forms #135/#236 (no legacy #128/#130, no address TLVs #132/#232); no MT-ISN #222 / #235 / #237; only 6-octet system-ids in typed bodies; no purge-originator (#13) or extended-sequence-number (#229) TLVs; no router-capability / SR TLVs. All are reachable byte-exact through the raw escape hatch (→ Backlog). Authentication (#10, RFC 5304/5310) is at parity with holo, plus FRR's opt-in `strict-rfc5310` keying and SHA-224, which holo does not configure.

## Scope

A **pure wire codec** for IS-IS PDUs and TLVs — the control-plane byte layer an
SPB (IEEE 802.1aq) fabric runs on. This module encodes and
decodes; it holds no state. The adjacency FSM, LSP database, flooding/SRM-SSN,
SPF, and the SPB tree computation are separate consumer modules built on top.

## Wire format

### Common header (ISO 10589 §9.1) — 8 octets

| Off | Field | Notes |
|-----|-------|-------|
| 0 | Intradomain Routing Protocol Discriminator | constant `0x83`; rejected otherwise |
| 1 | Length Indicator | length of the **fixed** header (common + type-specific): 20 (P2P IIH), 27 (LAN IIH / LSP), 33 (CSNP), 17 (PSNP). Not the total PDU length. |
| 2 | Version / Protocol ID Extension | constant `1` |
| 3 | ID Length | `0 ⇒ 6`, `255 ⇒ 0`, else literal. Normalized to `id_length` |
| 4 | R R R + PDU Type (low 5 bits) | reserved bits transmitted as zero, ignored on receipt |
| 5 | Version | constant `1` |
| 6 | Reserved | carried verbatim (soft field) |
| 7 | Maximum Area Addresses | `0 ⇒ 3` |

`header.decode` validates only these 8 octets, so a caller may decode a bare
common header. The upper bound on the Length Indicator (the type-specific header
must actually be present) is the **body** decoder's concern — each body verifies
`buf.len >= fixed_len` and returns `TruncatedBody` otherwise.

### PDU bodies

- **IIH LAN (15/16):** circuit-type, 6-octet source-id, holding-time, PDU-Length,
  7-bit priority, 7-octet LAN-ID (DIS). Fixed header 27.
- **IIH P2P (17):** circuit-type, source-id, holding-time, PDU-Length,
  local-circuit-id. Fixed header 20.
- **LSP (18/20):** PDU-Length, remaining-lifetime, 8-octet LSP-ID, 32-bit
  sequence-number, 16-bit checksum, flags octet (P / ATT×4 / OL / IS-Type).
  Fixed header 27.
- **CSNP (24/25):** PDU-Length, 7-octet source-id, start/end LSP-ID range.
  Fixed header 33.
- **PSNP (26/27):** PDU-Length, source-id. Fixed header 17.

Each body's **PDU Length** field is validated into `[fixed_len, buf.len]`; the
TLV region is exactly `buf[fixed_len .. pdu_length]`.

### TLVs

`code(1) length(1) value(length)`, walked by `tlv.TlvIterator`. Sub-TLVs are the
same shape nested inside a value (Extended IS Reachability #22; the SPB
MT-Capability #144 / MT-Port-Cap #143 containers). Modeled codes and their
sources:

| Code | Name | Source |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | Area Addresses | ISO 10589 |
| 2 | IS Neighbours (LSP, old-style) | ISO 10589 §9.8 |
| 6 | IS Neighbours (IIH SNPAs) | ISO 10589 §9.5/9.7 |
| 9 | LSP Entries (for CSNP/PSNP) | ISO 10589 §9.10 |
| 10 | Authentication (cleartext / HMAC-MD5 / RFC 5310 crypto) | ISO 10589 §9.5, RFC 5304, RFC 5310 |
| 22 | Extended IS Reachability (+ sub-TLVs) | RFC 5305 |
| 129 | Protocols Supported | RFC 1195 |
| 135 | Extended IP Reachability (+ sub-TLVs; prefix host bits masked) | RFC 5305 §4 |
| 236 | IPv6 Reachability (+ sub-TLVs; prefix host bits masked) | RFC 5308 §2 |
| 137 | Dynamic Hostname | RFC 5301 |
| 143 | MT-Port-Capability (SPB, IIH) | RFC 6165 / 6329 |
| 144 | MT-Capability (SPB, LSP) | RFC 6329 |

## SPB TLV layout + provenance of the numbers

All SPB numbers are from **RFC 6329** (IANA registrations), cross-checked
against the IANA IS-IS TLV and sub-TLV code-point registries:

- Container **MT-Capability = TLV 144** (in LSPs), **MT-Port-Capability = TLV 143**
  (in IIH). Both open with a 2-octet preamble: `O` (overload) bit, 3 reserved
  bits, 12-bit MT-ID — then a sub-TLV stream.
- **SPB Instance = sub-TLV 1** (of 144): 8-octet CIST Root Identifier, 4-octet
  CIST External Root Path Cost, 2-octet Bridge Priority, a 4-octet word
  `R(11) | V(1) | SPSourceID(20)`, 1-octet Num-of-Trees, then N × 8-octet
  ECT-VID tuples `U|M|A|Res(5) · ECT-ALGORITHM(32) · BaseVID(12)|SPVID(12)`.
- **SPBM Service Identifier and Unicast Address ("SPBM-SI") = sub-TLV 3**
  (of 144): 6-octet B-MAC, 2-octet `Res(4) | Base-VID(12)`, then N × 4-octet
  I-SID entries `T|R|Res(6) · I-SID(24)`. T = transmit-allowed, R =
  receive-allowed.

The bit orderings (V bit at position 20 of the SPB-Inst word; Base-VID in the
**low** 12 bits of the SPBM-SI 2-octet field; T/R as the two MSBs of each I-SID
entry) were taken from the verbatim RFC 6329 figures and are pinned in the LSP
golden. No number here is a guess; where a sub-TLV is not modeled it is named in
the raw-only list, not invented.

## Fletcher checksum

`checksum.compute(bytes, csum_off)` and `checksum.verify(bytes)` are the ISO 8473 Annex C / RFC 905 Annex B Fletcher checksum (`compute` returns `error{ChecksumFieldOutOfRange}!u16`). The LSP framing is in `pdu.lspChecksumRegion`, `computeLspChecksum`, `checkLspChecksum`, `stampLspChecksum` and `LspBuilder.finishStamped`: per ISO 10589 §7.3.11 the checksum covers all fields of the LSP after the Remaining Lifetime field. `Lsp.decode` carries the raw 16-bit field and validates nothing, so the zero-allocation decode contract is untouched. A zero field means "not computed" (`ChecksumStatus.not_present`); the receive policy built on that (§7.3.14.2's discard) belongs to the update process (`isis-lsdb`). The §7.3.11 hardware-failure precaution is not implemented (see *What is deliberately not done*).

## Threat model / untrusted decode

`decode` consumes bytes off an untrusted link (a hostile or buggy peer, or an
attacker who can inject frames). The central hazard of a TLV codec is an
**attacker-controlled length**. Defenses:

- **One length-check implementation.** Top-level TLVs and sub-TLVs both use
  `tlv.TlvIterator`; there is a single `value_start + len > buf.len` guard to
  audit. `len` is a `u8` (≤ 255) and the sum is `usize`, so it cannot wrap.
- **Zero allocation on decode.** Every `value`/`sub_tlvs`/`tlv_bytes` is a
  subslice of the input; a decode cannot allocate more than its input, by
  construction. The fuzz target asserts each yielded value lies strictly within
  the input `ptr..ptr+len`.
- **Guaranteed termination.** Each TLV step advances `pos` by ≥ 2. The typed
  record iterators (SNPA, IS-reach, LSP-entries, ECT-VID, I-SID) advance by
  their fixed record size and reject a partial trailing record. No walk can
  loop.
- **Bounded nesting.** The walker never recurses on itself; the typed decoders
  descend exactly one sub-TLV level, so a crafted PDU cannot induce unbounded
  recursion or stack growth.
- **Body length lies caught.** A PDU-Length below the fixed header or beyond the
  buffer is `BadPduLength`; a Length-Indicator below 8 is `BadLengthIndicator`;
  an SPB Num-of-Trees or I-SID run exceeding the sub-TLV value is `BadLength`.
- **Reserved fields follow ISO/IEC 10589:2002.** Reserved bits are transmitted
  as zero and ignored on receipt (the 3 high PDU-type bits, the 6 high
  Circuit Type bits). An IIH whose Circuit Type is the reserved value 0 is
  refused whole (`ReservedCircuitType`) — "if specified the entire PDU shall be
  ignored" — and `CircuitType` has no member a builder could emit it with.
  The quoted sentences are RFC 1142's (§9.1, §9.5-§9.9), the IETF republication
  of the ISO draft; the ISO/IEC 10589:2002 text itself has not been checked
  against them.

**Authentication (#10) — the codec signs and verifies, the policy is the caller's.**
`auth` types the Authentication TLV and computes/verifies it
over a whole PDU (`src/auth.zig`); decoding a PDU still does NOT verify
anything — `decode` carries #10 like any TLV, and a PDU is authenticated only
where a caller runs `auth.verify` on it (`isis-adj` for IIHs, `isis-lsdb` for
LSPs and SNPs, each when a key is configured). SPB integrity (RFC 6329 digest
exchange) stays out of scope. See § Authentication below.

## Authentication

**Wire.** Authentication Type octet, then: type 1 the cleartext password
(ISO 10589 §9.5); type 54 a 16-octet HMAC-MD5, TLV length exactly 17 (RFC
5304 §2); type 3 a 2-octet Key ID and an L-octet HMAC (RFC 5310 §3.1, SHA-1/
224/256/384/512). Any other type is carried as `.other` and `verify` refuses it
(`UnsupportedAuthType`).

**What the digest covers.** `[0, PDU Length)` with the Authentication Value
hashed as zeros (RFC 5304 §2) or as Apad = 0x878FE1F3 repeated L/4 times (RFC
5310 §3.3, §3.5), and in an LSP Remaining Lifetime and Checksum hashed as zero
(RFC 5304 §2; RFC 5310 §3.4/§3.5) — so an LSP can be aged in flight and its
checksum, which covers the digest, is stamped after signing (`sign` re-stamps
it). Octets beyond PDU Length are not covered. Hellos are signed as sent,
padding included (RFC 5310 §3.2). holo-isis (`pdu.rs`
`auth_compute_digest`) hashes the same segments.

**Key preparation — the RFC and the routers disagree.** RFC 5310 §3.3 sets
`Ko = H(K)` for a key longer than the hash OUTPUT length L; plain RFC 2104
HMAC hashes only a key longer than the BLOCK size B. Survey (2026-11-18):
holo-isis uses the `hmac` crate (plain RFC 2104); FRR pull request 23715
("isisd: key chain authentication (RFC 5310)"; its author reports the commits merged through pull request 23969) defaults
to plain HMAC and states that Cisco IOS XR, Arista EOS and holo "hash only
keys longer than the block", with an IOS XR hello signed by a 22-octet
HMAC-SHA-1 key that verified only with plain HMAC; FRR keeps the RFC rule as an
opt-in `strict-rfc5310` keyword. The RFC 5709 (OSPF, identical text) erratum
proposes the block-size reading. So the default here is plain RFC 2104 — the
majority of deployed implementations, the interop that matters — and
`Key.strict_rfc5310 = true` selects §3.3. The two agree for every key of at
most L octets and for every key longer than B (both hash it); they differ only
for L < |K| <= B (21..64 octets with SHA-1, 33..64 with SHA-256, 49..128 with
SHA-384). HMAC-MD5 (RFC 5304) is RFC 2104 by definition and ignores the flag.

**Receive.** The first #10 counts; a second one is hashed payload (holo skips
duplicates the same way). RFC 5310 picks the key by Key ID (§3.5); HMAC-MD5 and
cleartext try every configured key of that type (RFC 5304 §2: "MAY check a set
of passwords"). Errors are distinct — `AuthMissing`, `KeyNotFound`,
`UnsupportedAuthType`, `AuthFailed`, `MalformedAuth` (holo:
`AuthTypeMismatch`, `AuthKeyNotFound`, `AuthError`) — and the siblings drop the
PDU on every one. The compare is `std.crypto.timing_safe.eql` (HMAC-MD5) or a
constant-time XOR fold (variable L, cleartext); lengths, the Key ID and which
key is tried are public, and the boolean verdict is declassified for memcheck
(it is observable anyway: the PDU is used or dropped). Cleartext is supported
in both directions like holo and FRR, and is not authentication against
anyone who can read the link. Neither RFC protects against replay (RFC 5310
§4); purge rules (RFC 5304 §2, RFC 6233) are the update process's
(`isis-lsdb`).

**Key material.** `Key.secret` is caller-owned (CONVENTIONS §2.1 Z2); the
only copy this module makes is the strict-mode `Ko = H(K)`, a local wiped by
`defer`. The HMAC state is a transform's working state (Z3, not wiped, as in
std).

**Anchor.** `src/auth_kat_test.zig`: 13 KATs (every PDU kind, every algorithm,
cleartext, a 22-octet SHA-1 and a 40-octet SHA-256 key in both key
preparations, a 130-octet key longer than every block) produced by
`tools/auth_kat.py`, an independent recipe: PDUs assembled field by field,
Python `hmac`/`hashlib`, its own ISO 8473 checksum. The module's builders plus
`sign` reproduce every byte. RFC 5304/5310 publish no vectors and holo-isis
could not be run here, so the holo cross-check is by reading (same segments,
same Apad, same plain keying), not by execution.

## Verification

Offline only: a pure codec with no live-interop surface here. Run: `scripts/modtest isis`.

- **Goldens** (`src/goldens.zig`): PDUs pinned byte for byte in three directions: the builders reproduce the golden bytes, the decoders recover every field, and `encode(decode(golden)) == golden`. They are hand-assembled field by field from ISO 10589 / RFC 6329; five of the PDU bodies (including the L2 CSNP and PSNP) are also graded by an independent dissector (Wireshark's `sharkd`), whose verdicts the file records. The Length-Indicator / PDU-Length constants (20 / 27 / 37 / 60) are a cross-check on the hand assembly.
- **Checksum:** `checksum.zig` is anchored on Wireshark's own Fletcher implementation: the same octets graded `Good` (0xaee7) and `Bad` (0x1111) by `sharkd`. This is the strongest external anchor the module has.
- **Round trip:** encode and decode over empty TLV sets, max-length (255) and zero-length TLVs, repeated same-code TLVs, and the raw escape hatch (an unmodeled type re-emits verbatim).
- **Bounds safety:** truncated headers, overrunning TLV lengths, a lying body PDU-Length, oversize builder values, partial trailing records in every typed iterator, the SPB sub-length lies. Permanent positive control: `tlv.zig` proves a length-trusting walk would over-read where the safe walk returns `TruncatedTlv`, so the test goes red when the guard is removed.
- **Fuzz:** deterministic driver `ISIS_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` (harness `isis-decode`, `src/fuzz_test.zig`; also a `std.testing.fuzz` target) over the dispatch decoder, the raw and sub-TLV walks, the typed sub-decoders and the LSP checksum entry points, asserting never-panic, walk termination and value-within-input. The input draw biases a full modeled header and a consistent PDU-Length field, because random bytes alone are refused by `checkCommon`; a non-fuzz test ("fuzz harness: decode, 500 seeds, reaches every outcome") asserts the harness reaches a PDU body and every outcome.
- **Authentication:** `src/auth_kat_test.zig` against KATs produced by `tools/auth_kat.py` (see Authentication, Anchor); strict and plain key preparation, the key-selection and cross-algorithm refusals.
- **Mutation:** whole-module over every non-test line of `checksum.zig`, `header.zig`, `tlv.zig`, `tlvs.zig`, `pdu.zig`, `spb.zig` and the dispatch in `root.zig` (one mutant per condition and class; not mutated: comptime constants, the `catch unreachable` after a checked length, formatting, doc comments), plus a delta run over `auth.zig`. `src/mutation_test.zig` holds the tests added to kill survivors (exact-fit and one-short buffers, the fixed-header edge, byte orders, flag bits, partial trailing records, dispatch arms). The equivalent mutants: an exact 255-octet scratch fit no loop value can reach, redundant area-length tests, an iterator end test on a position that never exceeds the length, the PDU-length zeroing writes in the builders' `init` (`finish` overwrites the field), a byte-order mutant on a value only compared with zero, two guards in `encodeSpbInstance` that the builder repeats. No survivor sits in the checksum arithmetic, `verify`, the zero-checksum test or any auth or length check.
- **ctgrind** (`src/ctgrind_harness.zig`): targets `md5` and `sha256` (plain and strict RFC 5310 key preparation), key tainted, ReleaseFast: 0 contexts in module files on x86_64 native and on the portable build; rows in `scripts/checks/ctgrind-expected.tsv`. The harness also has a `clear` arm (cleartext password) that is not a ctgrind target: its taint reaches no reported context, so a row would measure nothing, and a cleartext password travels in the PDU anyway.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## What is deliberately not done

- **All protocol state:** the adjacency FSM, the LSP database, flooding (SRM/SSN; the CSNP/PSNP PDUs are modeled, the exchange algorithm is not), SPF and the SPB tree / ECT computation. This module supplies the bytes those consumers exchange.
- **ISO 10589 §7.3.11's hardware-failure precaution for checksum generation** (start from C0/C1 stored when the Network entity is enabled and whenever the systemID changes): a redundancy check against a corrupted in-memory systemID that needs persistent state this stateless codec does not hold. The wire value is unaffected, since resuming from a matching cached prefix equals one continuous pass. Full citation: `pdu.lsp_checksum_base`.
- **The SPB digest (RFC 6329) integrity exchange.**
- **The long tail of the IANA TLV registry** (IP Interface Address #132, TE sub-TLVs, segment routing, and so on) and the unmodeled SPB sub-TLVs (SPB-Inst-Opaque, SPBV, SPB-MCID, SPB-Digest, SPB-B-VID): reachable and byte-exact through the raw escape hatch; modeling any is additive. The ones that matter are in the Backlog.

## Backlog / deferred

- **The rest of the IP TLVs:** legacy #128/#130 reachability and the address TLVs #132 / #232 (the wide #135 and #236 are typed). Why: FRR carries the legacy forms with narrow metrics. Fits CONVENTIONS §2: yes (pure codec).
- **Purge Originator Identification (#13, RFC 6232) and Extended Sequence Number (#229, RFC 7602).** Why: FRR and holo emit and consume them; a purge without #13 cannot be traced. Effort: ~1 day.
- **Non-default ID length in typed bodies (ISO 10589 ID Length 1-8).** Today only 6 is wired and the rest return `UnsupportedIdLength`; the raw TLV walk is id-length-independent. Why: interop with the rare non-6 deployment. Effort: ~2 days, touches every fixed-offset read. Priority low.
- **MT TLVs #222 / #235 / #237** (multi-topology IS-IS, RFC 5120; only the MT-ID of #143/#144 is parsed today). Effort: ~2 days. Priority low.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle MIXED

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle MIXED** — anchored for some paths, self for others — the evidence below names which.

**What the tests actually contain.** Wireshark sharkd validated 5 PDU bodies + TLVs incl. L2 CSNP/PSNP (goldens.zig); long-tail raw-TLV escape hatch stays self-tested
